title: You are my father
hookLine: You are my father, You are my mother, You my kin and my brother (Majh M5, ang 103)

cards: Brother. Four plain family words, one after another: that's how this hymn of Guru Arjan opens. A child could sing that list after one hearing.
An adult sitting in a hospital corridor at three in the morning could say it too, and mean something a child can't yet know. The words stay the same; the person singing them keeps changing.

teach.b: The shabad is in Raag Majh, on ang 103. It begins, in effect: You are my father, You are my mother. You are my kin, You are my brother.
You are my protector in every place, so what fear, what worry, can touch me? The second stanza: by Your grace I come to know You. You are my shelter, You are my honor.
Without You there is no other; all of this is Your play, Your arena.

teach.h: OT AND MAAN, AS IN THE ARDAS.
teach.b: Listen for two words there: ot, shelter, and maan, honor. We met them in the Ardas three weeks ago: the honor of the dishonored, the shelter of the shelterless.
Here Guru Arjan says them in the first person: You are my shelter, You are my honor. Why family words? Guru Arjan had a father and mother.
He had brothers, and one of them, Prithi Chand, tradition says, kept back his letters home. Families hold the deepest love and sometimes the deepest hurt, and the shabad doesn't pretend otherwise.

teach.h: SO WHAT FEAR CAN TOUCH ME?
teach.b: What it does is name the One as every kind of family at once: the father who provides, the mother who holds, the kin who belong to you, the brother who stands next to you.
Whatever a person has or lacks in their own family, the hymn offers the same thing: you are not without family. And from there it reasons straight to fearlessness.
If the One is all of these, everywhere, fear has nowhere to stand. That's not a promise that nothing hard will happen. In the hymn, it's a promise about who is there when it does.

how: Guru Arjan's 'toon meraa pitaa toonhai meraa maataa' is sung in kirtan, taught to children, and turned to in times of trouble.

o: an elder brother who stands by you
father, one of the One's family names
a protector who guards every place

games.q: you are my father — tap the pairs.

s: the shabad names the One as mother as well as father
You are my father, You are my mother: both in the opening line.
the shabad uses ot and maan, words from the Ardas
You are my shelter, You are my honor.
the shabad is by Guru Nanak
it is Guru Arjan's, in Raag Majh, on ang 103.

games.q: Guru Arjan has named the One as father, mother, kin and brother. what does he conclude?
o: so I need no human family.
so what fear or worry can touch me?
so I must earn this love.
games.why: You are my protector in every place, so what fear can I have? the family words lead to fearlessness.

practice: Let the family words come one at a time, father, mother, kin, brother, and with each, notice what rises: warmth, ache, absence, gratitude, whatever it is.
If you pray, you can say the line to the One slowly, in English or Punjabi: You are my father, You are my mother.
If you don't, simply rest with the thought that you are not without family, and let one person who has been family to you come to mind.

wordCard.voice: Pitaa, father: Guru Arjan names the One as pitaa, mother, kin and brother, protector everywhere, and asks, so what fear can touch me?

orig.note: Gurmukhi: father; the shabad opens tooN meraa pitaa, You are my father.

carryVoice: Your line: you are my family. Ot and maan, shelter and honor, said in the first person. Six hundred fifty-three days, and counting.
